evals.prompt: Add a --dry-run flag to the CLI with tests, update the README section that lists the flags, and commit the result.
evals.expected_output: Before any work, the agent splits the request into three deliverables and routes the flag and tests as implement to gpt-6.1-sol at high effort, the README section as write to claude-sonnet-5-5 at high effort, and the commit as operate to gpt-6-luna at high effort, then identifies the harness and checks each selected model and effort before starting, recording any unavailable runtime verification as an unverified route.
expectations: The agent classifies the deliverables by purpose before writing code or delegating

The flag implementation and its tests are classified as implement and routed to gpt-6.1-sol with high effort; argparse help strings and running the tests stay inside that deliverable without a model switch
The README update is classified as write and routed to claude-sonnet-5-5 with high effort, separately from the implementation, without escalation merely because it lands in a committed file
The commit is classified as operate and routed to gpt-6-luna with high effort
The agent identifies the current harness and resolves each model ID and effort setting against its catalog before switching or launching
Each route line records the category and source, the selected model ID, verification source or gap, harness, effort, and session identifier or none

When runtime verification is unavailable after explicit model and effort selection, the agent records an unverified route; a failed selection or a mismatched model or effort is corrected with a verified setting or takes the next applicable execution path
evals.baseline: Without the skill the agent did everything itself on claude-fable-5-1: it added --dry-run to cli.py, wrote five tests, extended the README Flags list, and committed as 'feat: add --dry-run flag to list files without deleting them'. It never split the request into deliverables, named no model, did not identify the harness or consult any catalog, launched no other session, and recorded no route, so every expectation about routing to gpt-6.1-sol, claude-opus-5-5, and gpt-6-luna and about route records fell short. The orchestrator seeded the workspace with a small argparse CLI, a unittest suite, and a README with a Flags section because the evaluation supplies no fixtures.

runs.notes: All expectations held. The subagent read the skill, classified the three deliverables before touching code, identified the harness as Claude Code under T3 Code on claude-fable-5-1, and, because a Claude Code subagent cannot switch its own model and the Agent tool only takes Anthropic aliases, used the external codex CLI for the OpenAI routes: flag and tests on codex session 01a114bb-a801-7291-9e36-b1d386a3fb4e (rollout metadata model gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning_effort high, confirmed by the orchestrator), help text and README bullet on an Agent sub-session with alias opus whose launch result reported claude-opus-5-5, commit on codex session 01a114bd-ddbd-7a31-a60e-2fb3468cafd1 (rollout metadata gpt-6-luna, effort high). All three routes were recorded in the skill's form with model, verification source, harness, effort, and session. The first Luna commit attempt failed because the codex workspace-write sandbox keeps .git read-only; the agent resumed the same session with the sandbox bypassed instead of changing model, and commit 2923219 'feat: add --dry-run flag' landed with README, cli.py, and tests. No route needed the unverified marker. Observation: the codex workers loaded model-routing themselves and the Sol worker spawned a child thread, also on gpt-6.1-sol.

Codex read ~/.agents/skills/model-routing/SKILL.md and stated the three routes before working, but then performed the Development part itself. Failed: 'The flag implementation and its tests are routed to gpt-6.1-sol': the gpt-6-astra exec session edited cli.py and tests/test_cli.py directly and never launched a gpt-6.1-sol session. Failed: 'The commit is routed to gpt-6-luna': no Luna session was started; the agent only noted that .git is read-only inside the workspace-write sandbox and left the changes uncommitted. Failed: 'Each route records the selected model ID, verification source or gap, harness, effort setting or unsupported, and session identifier or none': no route line in the skill's form appeared; the final message was prose ('Blocked by two issues') rather than the Blocked/Attempts/Needed report. Held: classification before work; the README was routed separately to claude-opus-5-5 via 'claude --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high -p', which failed with EAI_AGAIN because the codex sandbox has no network, after which the agent asked the user whether gpt-6.1-sol may write the prose instead. README unchanged, partial --dry-run in the working tree, 3 tests passing.

OpenCode loaded the skill via its Skill tool and stated the routes (implementation and tests to GPT 6.1 Sol, README and help text to Claude Opus 5.5, commit to GPT 6 Luna) before any work, then ran command -v, opencode --help, opencode models, opencode session list, codex --help, claude --help, codex login status, codex agents --help, and claude auth status. Its next two tool calls, read on /home/agent/.codex and /home/agent/.claude, were rejected by the non-interactive permission system and the session ended with finish reason tool-calls, no final message, and the workspace untouched (exit code 0). Failed: 'The flag implementation and its tests are routed to gpt-6.1-sol', 'The README update is routed to claude-opus-5-5 as prose shipped with a Development change, separately from the implementation', 'The commit is routed to gpt-6-luna': no session was launched for any deliverable and nothing was produced. Failed: 'The agent identifies the current harness and resolves each model ID against its catalog before switching or launching': it listed the opencode catalog but never resolved or launched. Failed: 'Each route records the selected model ID, verification source or gap, harness, effort setting or unsupported, and session identifier or none' and the Blocked report: no route record and no report, because the run ended silently. Held: classification before writing code or delegating.
